messages.author: edc716aa20496f25
messages.subject: simulate time to detection data in R
parts:
Howdy, I'm trying to simulate ttd data (without using simoccttd) but get lots of NAs. Any idea what I should be doing?

#simulate data
M=250
lambda=0.3
psi=0.4
Tmax=10
y<-matrix(NA, ncol=Tmax, nrow=M)
z<-rexp(n=M, rate=lambda)
for (j in 1:Tmax){
  y[,j]<-rbinom(n=M, size=1, prob=(z*psi))
}

messages.author: daaeb91800c54fd1
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] simulate time to detection data in R
parts:
What if you tried something like this:

M=250
lambda=0.3
psi=0.4
Tmax=10  
z <- rbinom(M, 1, psi )                               # True Occupancy
t.rand <- rexp(M, rate = lambda)               # Random Time to First Detection based on lambda
time.det <- ifelse(t.rand <= Tmax & z == 1, t.rand, NA)              # Observed Time to First Detection
detect <- 1 * is.finite(time.det)

Jesse

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] simulate time to detection data in R
parts: It all works nicely but I tweaked 'd' to run in model 10.12.1 in Kery & Royle. And while it produces similar output to their simulation from simOccttd the results from the JAGS model (below)are odd. I removed the covariates aplha1 & beta1 from the model thinking this is OK. Perhaps not? If anyone has any other ideas that would be good.

M=250
lambda=0.3
psi=0.4
Tmax=10
z <- rbinom(M, 1, psi )                               # True Occupancy
t.rand <- rexp(M, rate = lambda)               # Random Time to First Detection based on lambda

time.det <- ifelse(t.rand <= Tmax & z == 1, t.rand, NA)              # Observed Time to First Detection. Perhaps round if time units finite.
d <- as.numeric(is.na(time.det))    # Censoring indicator
hist(time.det, breaks=50) 

# 10.12.1 Occupancy models with "survival model" observation process:
#         exponential time-to-detection (TTD) model with simulated data

modelstring="
model{
# Priors
int.psi ~ dunif(0, 1)               # Intercept occupancy on prob. scale
int.lambda ~ dgamma(0.0001, 0.0001) # Poisson rate parameter
beta1~dnorm(0,0.001)
alpha1~dnorm(0,0.001)
# Likelihood
for (i in 1:nobs){
# Model for occurrence
z[i] ~ dbern(psi[i])
logit(psi[i])<-logit(int.psi+beta1)
#logit(psi[i])<-logit(int.psi)                #without beta

# Observation model
# Exponential model for time to detection ignoring censoring
ttd[i] ~ dexp(lambda[i])
log(lambda[i])<-log(int.lambda+alpha1)
#log(lambda[i])<-log(int.lambda)             #without alpha
# Model for censoring due to species absence and ttd>=Tmax
d[i] ~ dbern(theta[i])                                             #d <- as.numeric(is.na(data$ttd))    # Censoring indicator
theta[i] <- z[i] * step(ttd[i] - Tmax) + (1 - z[i])
}
# Derived quantities
n.occ <- sum(z[])                   # Number of occupied sites
}
"
writeLines(modelstring, con="model.txt")

messages.author: daaeb91800c54fd1
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] simulate time to detection data in R
parts:
A couple things to try:
Use normal priors for int.psi, int.lambda, beta1, and alpha1.
logit(psi[i])<- int.psi+beta1 * data.beta1[i]                     # you require data for your covariate, or remove the term beta1.  Also you don't want 'logit' on both sides of your equation.
lambda[i] <- exp(int.lambda + alpha1 * data.alpha[i])   # you require data for your covariate, or remove the term alpha1.  Also don't want the 'log' transformation on both sides of your equation.

Hope this helps,
Jesse
